content.title: Battle of Bạch Đằng, 1288

phases.title: Preparing the terrain
phases.narrative: Defenders used the river environment, stake field, and tide timing as coordinated conditions. Specific placement is simplified so a hypothesis is not presented as settled fact.
assumptions: The stake-field position in the diagram is an approximate locator.

phases.title: The fleet withdraws with the tide
phases.narrative: The fleet withdraws into the river while conditions remain favourable. The arrow marks narrative direction, not speed, force size, or formation.
assumptions: Movement direction is abstracted from common accounts; it is not a complete battle map.

phases.title: Counterattack as conditions change
phases.narrative: As the tide ebbs, the stake field and river forces create difficult conditions for the withdrawing fleet. The reconstruction does not simulate collisions, casualties, or outcomes through physics.
assumptions: The relationship among tide, stakes, and outcome is presented as a sourced interpretation.

fallback.narrative: In 1288, Trần forces organised defence in the Bạch Đằng river environment. This reconstruction divides the account into three phases: preparing the terrain, a withdrawing fleet following the tide, and a counterattack as conditions changed. Arrows are educational locators; the full narrative, sources, and assumptions remain available without WebGL.
